sector: Retail/e-commerce last-mile delivery (Saudi Arabia; pooled courier fleets and parcel lockers)
hitl_conditions: Not discussed explicitly; the pipeline is offline and advisory, so managers keep dispatch/planning decisions. Real-time autonomous control (RL-based dispatching on OpenStreetMap networks) is deferred to future work, which would shift dispatch away from humans.
key_finding: Gradient-boosting demand/ETA forecasts (LightGBM, CatBoost, SHAP) feed OR-Tools VRP-TW routing and CP-SAT locker siting; a SimPy 'Level-1' digital twin only stress-tests these policies. Pooled fleets cut routing cost 65% and lift on-time delivery from 37% to 100%; 25 lockers cut CO2 to 0.06 kg/parcel; SLA holds under Ramadan/weather stress.
citation_locator: Key finding: Abstract Methods/Results (printed p. 199, PDF p. 1); Methods 'Digital Twin Simulation (SimPy)' (p. 204, PDF p. 6); Results (pp. 205-208, PDF pp. 7-10: Table 3 'SimPy Twin' rows and Table 4 on p. 207, Table 5 and stress-test paragraph on p. 208). Twin claim: keywords and Abstract (p. 199), Introduction contribution 4 (p. 200), Methods heading (p. 204), Conclusion 'A Level-1 digital twin' (p. 209, PDF p. 11); synthetic customer population acknowledged in Results (p. 208) and Discussion (p. 209). HITL evidence: Abstract Conclusions and Literature review ('actionable insights for logistics managers/operators, urban planners, and policymakers', pp. 199 and 201); Conclusion practical implications (pp. 209-210: managers integrating demand forecasting into daily fleet dispatch) and Conclusion future work (p. 209: reinforcement-learning-based dispatching for adaptive, real-time fleet control). No dispatcher or platform-operator role in the loop is described anywhere; 'operators' means fleet-owning logistics firms whose fleets are pooled (Methods p. 203, Discussion p. 209).

quotes.text: The interaction between forecasts, routing decisions, and facility siting is validated using a digital twin implemented with SimPy. Orders are generated stochastically based on demand forecasts, while couriers, lockers, and vehicles are modeled as resources subject to capacity constraints.
quotes.section: Methods – Digital Twin Simulation (SimPy) (printed p. 204; PDF p. 6)

quotes.text: This study proposes a machine learning–driven smart-sharing framework that integrates predictive analytics with operations research to optimize last-mile delivery in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

Demand forecasting models (SARIMAX, XGBoost, LightGBM) capture temporal and event-driven variations, while ETA prediction models (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost with SHAP explainability) refine delivery time estimates. Routing decisions are solved as a VRP-TW with OR-Tools, extended by locker siting through CP-SAT.
quotes.section: Methods – Digital Twin Simulation (SimPy), closing summary paragraph (printed p. 204; PDF p. 6)

quotes.text: A Level-1 digital twin was used to validate system resilience under stress scenarios.
Future work should incorporate real OpenStreetMap networks and reinforcement-learning-based dispatching to enable adaptive, real-time fleet control.
quotes.section: Conclusion, future work (printed p. 209; PDF p. 11)

quotes.text: From a practical perspective, logistics managers may benefit from integrating demand forecasting into daily fleet dispatch

IA = gradient boosting predictivo; lo prescriptivo es OR (nivel 3 en lectura estricta). Humano sólo receptor de 'insights' (cabría 'Maintained'); despacho autónomo por RL es trabajo futuro.
